# tezc/sc: diagnosing 22 injected faults without a test suite

The repository has received 22 separate undocumented edits.

This is a grab bag of small building blocks that programs lean on for everyday work: pulling
apart text that arrived from somewhere else, assembling text and bytes to hand back, keeping
items and giving them out in a chosen order, and arranging for work to happen later. A program
built on it now gets a number of these wrong. Nothing about the inputs changed and nothing
about the callers changed. The same calls that used to come back right now come back wrong,
and in several places a call that used to succeed now reports failure or dies outright.

Taking apart text that arrived from somewhere else. Pulling a web address apart when it carries
both a query part and a fragment hands back a query whose text and length do not cover the
characters between the question mark and the hash, and the fragment beside it is wrong as well.
Feeding configuration text holding several entries yields entries for only part of what was fed
in, because the division between one entry and the next falls in the wrong place, so key and
value pairs come back run together or are never reported. An entry whose value is trailed by
wording meant for a human reader comes back with that wording or the blank space in front of it
still attached, or with characters of the value cut off. Converting a human-readable amount of
